newsitem.title: USA: Gap earnings, sales rise in final quarter.
newsitem.headline: Gap earnings, sales rise in final quarter.

text.p: Gap Inc. reported record earnings Thursday for its final quarter on a 10 percent increase in sales and announced the opening of at least 275 stores in all its divisions.
Gap, which owns Gap, GapKids, Banana Republic and Old Navy stores, said it opened 203 new stores in 1996, and the number of 1997 openings represents a "substantial" increase.

"Our results demonstrate the strength of our balanced portfolio of apparel brands, with Gap, Banana Republic and Old Navy all improving their profitability in 1996," said Millard S. Drexler, Gap Inc. president and chief executive officer.
He said the company's earnings per share have grown at a compound annual rate of 22 percent over the last three years and 21 percent over the last 10 years.
For the quarter, Gap earned $171.2 million, or 62 cents a share, on sales of $1.67 billion. A year earlier it earned $154.6 million, or 54 cents a share, on sales of $1.52 billion.
For the year, Gap earned $152.9 million, or $1.60 a share, on sales of $5.28 billion. A year earlier it earned $354.0 million, or $1.23 a share, on sales of $4.39 billion a year earlier.
"We remain committed to increasing shareholder returns, through a combination of an active share repurchase programme and growth in all our core businesses," Dexter said.
Last year Gap operated 1,854 stores, including 938 Gap, 226 Banana Republic, 497 GapKids and 193 Old Navy stores.
Gap stock was off 87.5 cents at $33.375 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
